utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: This afternoon we're late in starting because the previous trial unavoidably overran its time. Let the witness make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may sit. And you may begin, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. As this witness has all manner of protective measures, can he be shown this document for his identification?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this is me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Apologies for this short break, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Sorry for the interruption. Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now tell us, sir, what was your job like in the period from 1992 through to the end of 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I worked as a photographer and cameraman under very difficult circumstances, quite stressful. I documented these events, and very often I found myself in dangerous situations. I was even injured. These were very, very hard times, and my job was a difficult one to perform. But I did everything I could in order to avoid carrying a rifle. I didn't even wear my uniform unless there was a meeting of sorts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I forgot to thank you. You came here with a fractured leg in order to be helpful to this Tribunal with your testimony. You've just mentioned stressful situations. Before I move on to the photographs you made, can you tell us which of these stressful situations remains stuck in your memory in these past years?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: There were very many such instances. I produced quite a voluminous archives. I have 12.000 photographs that I made. When I spoke to the lawyer for the first time, I was told that they were interested in the period from the month of August of 1994 onwards, and I picked out some of the photographs as far as I was able to. However, the most stressful situation to me was when two little girls were killed at Grbavica. And there was another instance involving two young people, Boro and Admira and they were killed as they were crossing the bridge. I attended their funeral. There were their mothers there. In addition to that I had personal problems, private problems because as a photographer I was assigned to make photographs of some exhumed soldiers and civilians. This was very hard to me. I had to make photographs that would enable individuals to identify them. On one occasion there were 40 bodies of persons exhumed that I had to make photographs of. I did not touch the archives that I had for 10 years. I did not go back and look at them because I found it so difficult to remind myself of these events.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Let me start with the photographs. What did I ask you to do as you just mentioned? Which were the photographs that you were asked to produce and examine? Did you make each and every one of these photographs yourself, and whatever can be seen in these photographs is something that saw with your own eyes; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes. All these are my photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Well, it's been answered, but my submission was that it's a leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, I doubt that, but proceed, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us start from the photographs and look in each and every one of them and each time I will ask you if you made each and every photograph, but let me make this preliminary question to you: Do you know when was it that Dragomir Milosevic, the accused in this case, became commander of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: It was in early August of 1994 that I learnt that Dragomir Milosevic had become the commander of the corps or, rather, that he had been appointed. I don't know what the procedure involved was. I only know that this was in that time period.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the photograph DD004229 be shown. Your Honours, all these photographs are the ones taken from the large batch of photographs that were already shown to some of the witnesses. Since this particular once made these photographs, he will comment on the photographs that I have selected. He will give you his observations, contemporaneous ones. So this first photograph is DD004229. I only provided the Prosecution with some of the photographs in the past days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, what will be the evidential value of these photographs?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I cannot tell you that until you see the photographs themselves. They have to do with sniper fire, with hills we referred to, with the positions below the hills. These are photographs featuring civilians, who were wounded or killed, lying on the ground. The photographs speak to all the matters that I raised in these past weeks. The photographs show what the results of the activities of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina were during the critical period. These were sites that were exposed to sniper fire. There are matters that you will see for the first time there. For example, Debelo Brdo, a picture of which was taken from a different angle, then the road leading across Zlatiste.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: All right. Let us see the first one.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There seems to be a technical difficulty here. They are in the e-court, but we can't seem to be able to call them up. Perhaps we should use the ELMO. That might make it simpler.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you look at the photograph, can you tell us were you an eyewitness to the sniper fire or gunfire being opened upon certain sites, and did you document that? Did you film that or make photographs of that? Can you tell us this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes. I was an eyewitness of that. I was there, and I made these photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again I don't have the photograph here in front of me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look at the photograph now, please. You said that you were an eyewitness to sniper fire or gunfire. Can you tell the Judges what these photographs depict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: These photographs I made in the Dobrinja settlement. The top photograph depicts a man entering a building, whereas on the right-hand side you can see concrete block obstacles that are actually screens from snipers, enabling persons to enter the building. The bottom photograph shows the building which stands opposite the building depicted on the top photograph. You can see bullet-holes made by sniper fire. I don't know whether I should point to these holes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please circle them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have them in e-court now, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: You see there one beneath the balcony, and down there where the staircase is you simply make an aperture there, a little hole enabling you to open fire. It's very difficult to protect oneself from such fire. You have to use barricades, some sort of optical visibility barriers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where is this building located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I can't see it now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is this building situated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: At Dobrinja, practically on the line of separation. There was only one road dividing two buildings, and in one building there were ABiH soldiers and in the other the VRS soldiers. I believe the name of the street is Indira Gandhi Street. I'm not 100 per cent sure. These apertures that would appear overnight in the stairwells or elsewhere posed a great threat, and one had to move around with great caution. One never knew where the sniper fire might come from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in what way did the citizens protect themselves from such sniper fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: The only way to protect oneself was to erect screens from whatever material was available so that snipers could not see you as you were moving through the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see snipers as they opened fire?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Did you, Mr. Witness, yourself witness any of these shots being made?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know that every time I approached that area I was warned, and people said shots were fired from this or that building one or two days ago and one was hit. In another area in Grbavica I was present when a 15-year-old girl was hit in the leg by a sniper from one of those holes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: The reason I put the question was that I needed to find out just how the Chamber would ascertain that these were sniper fire bullets and not just shots that part of the armed conflict between combatants.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was not trying to suggest snipers or insist on it, or whether it was snipers or something else that was being used, but only that shots were fired through these holes, and that's why the witness took these photographs. That's why screens were erected where these holes were. And you will see a picture of another building Your Honours also visited during the site visit from which shots were fired in a similar way. I tender this photograph as a Defence exhibit, and I will show only one similar picture. I have others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... It has little evidential value in my view. He took the photographs, so I believe we can admit it, but I don't see how much weight, if any, can be attached to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, please, on this first photograph did you remember what year you took it, and who is that person that we see? Don't give us the name, just tell us if you know who the person is and why you actually took this picture. What was the purpose of you taking this picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This photograph was taken in the winter of 1994. I was sent there. The army invited someone to take photographs of those holes so that one could see that these were small holes which were being used for sniper fire. As for this person, I know that person. He was a kind of courier taking food to the soldiers. I didn't dare approach the building on my own. I needed an escort, and this man took me there and said, "We will stay here very briefly." And I took the photograph hastily. You can see that it was taken from a window. This other man accompanied me, and I took the photographs to the press centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, maybe there was a slight imprecision in the interpretation, because if we return to the second picture below, your testimony in the English version says that these were holes -- bullet-holes made by sniper fire, but I'm now in doubt as to whether these were really holes through which sniping was made. So is it incoming holes or outgoing holes?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, let the witness explain. It may be what the record says, but that's not what the witness said. So let the witness explain. I don't want to lead in any way. Let the witness explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I was putting my question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I am objecting, because that's what the witness said. It was a misinterpretation. The witness said that these were holes which were made so people could fire through them. I don't know -- I'm very surprised at what the record says, because in B/C/S the witness said very clearly that these were holes which were made so that one could fire through them. They were not made by sniper fire. So I need to brush up my English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You're not in a position to object to the Judge's question. Let the witness explain what he said. What did you say, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that these holes were made by someone digging through the wall from the inside. One can see that the hole was made from the inside of the building so that a barrel could be pushed through the hole of a sniper or a rifle and one could shoot at soldiers or civilians through it. And the only protection was to erect screens so as not to be seen from these holes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, continue. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The man entering the building who can be seen here --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- what was the position of the building that man entered in relation to this one we see here with the holes in it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: The buildings faced each other, and where this man is going in, on the right-hand side you can see that from Mojmilo it was possible to fire on the area between the two buildings so a wall had to be erected there. And the building that was on the Bosniak side, from that building one could fire on this building. If people were not cautious enough in moving about, they were in danger of being hit from a sniper from -- firing from these holes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or maybe some other weapon could be used. But please tell us, I have to ask you directly now, what army did this building belong to, the one facing the building that man entered?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: It belonged to the army Bosnia-Herzegovina. These buildings are still there. They've been repaired. That's all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wish to tender this photograph, and it's up to Your Honours to decide whether it has any weight, but I feel it is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D323, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Before I show some photographs showing persons who have been hit by something in the streets, I wish to show a photograph of a building with similar characteristics to this one but it's one of the best known buildings in Sarajevo. That's D004228.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, what building is this? Does it have a name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: This is a building in Sarajevo on the right bank of the Miljacka opposite Grbavica. It's the building of the faculty of mathematics and natural sciences. The side facing Bosna did not have any windows. And throughout the war anyone who passed by along Grbavica, including myself, we were always afraid of these holes in the building which were made overnight. In the night they would make a hole, and then on the next day they would fire with snipers all over Grbavica. And we had to find out where the sniper was shooting from so that we could erect screens, because that was the only way to protect ourselves from sniper fire coming from this building. Many people fell victim here, especially until we discovered from where the sniper was firing at Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it says that this is the side facing the Miljacka, not the Bosna, as the record says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And those dots around the most conspicuous circle, what are those? Do you know what happened when fire was opened from those places? But before you say that, tell us when did you take this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: This was in September, I think, 1994. Although there were some holes in this building that were made in this building before, but new holes kept appearing. And the hole in the middle, that's where the stairwell was. That was the first hole that appeared. And then they shot from Grbavica, from the Serb side. You can see a lot of little holes because they were trying to neutralise the fire coming from that hole, and then there was no other way to deal with it but simply to put up screens to prevent people being seen, because there was no other way to protect oneself from that sniper. And it must be noted that when we protected one area, when we knew there was a hole through which a sniper was firing, they dug new holes in new places to fire at another area which then we would have to protect again and put up screens made up of different materials. I was terrified of this building because I was not in contact with those people every day, and I thought a new hole might be opened up controlling some new area that I didn't know about where I would have to run and hide and find shelters. I was afraid of being seen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tapuskovic, in the transcript, at page 14, line 13, it says that shots came from Grbavica, from the Serb side. It came from Grbavica from the Serb side. Is that what the witness meant at page 14, line 13? Is that exactly what he meant?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those little holes were rifle shots fired to neutralise that big hole in the middle. The shots came from the Serb side. That's what the witness said. Rifle shots were aimed at this first hole that appeared in order to neutralise it, and then new holes kept appearing. That's what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. But this building, was it located in the territory controlled by SRK or in the territory controlled by ABiH?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course I will ask the witness that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On whose territory was this building? You said it faced the Miljacka, but on whose territory was it? On whose territory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: This building was on the Bosniak side. It was on the right hand -- the right side of the river Miljacka. On the left-hand side was Grbavica, the Serb-controlled area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tell us once again what the name of the building was. What was this building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: This was the building of the faculty of mathematics and natural sciences in Sarajevo. I think it was in Vojvode Putnika street. I don't know the name of the house number. The name of the street then was Vojvode Putnika street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, did you hear or see the fire that gave rise to these holes in the building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These holes in the building were dug from the inside of the building out. You can see that they pushed out parts of the building material, and then they fired on Serb positions, both soldiers and civilians, from those holes. The first hole when it appeared, from the Serb side they tried to neutralise it by firing at it from rifles. So you can see that the facade is damaged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But are there any holes showing the fire from the Serb side that hit the building, or do you have no evidence as to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's evident here that an aperture was made from the inside. The only holes made from the Serb side are those little dots on the facade which are a result of rifle fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Are you able to say exactly when you made -- you took these photographs and, if possible, how soon after either, A, the holes were made allowing the ABiH to fire through them, or how soon after the holes were made resulting from fire from the SRK?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This photograph was made toward the end of the war. That was when I photographed the building. However, I photographed the building earlier on as well. This hole in the middle of the building appeared, I believe, in the summer of 1993. As soon as there was no more fog, there was no more winter, you would see these apertures appearing. I believe that this photograph was made sometime in May 1995. However, I have photographs that only show two or three holes. As I saw these holes appearing from the inside, I made photographs of the building. You can see that the photograph is a bit lopsided, as I took it in haste trying not to linger in the area for too long.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the transcript does not reflect --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in answer to your question, at the very end he said, "You see this photograph is a bit lopsided. I had to seek shelter because I was afraid that I might be shot," and this part has not been entered in the transcript at all. I believe that such important matters must not be left out of the transcript. I cannot follow English sufficiently well, but this is what he said and was not reflected in the transcript. Can I just ask the witness the following --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I heard that. I heard what you just said, and it should have been in the transcript. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But this is in the transcript, Mr. Tapuskovic. It is in the transcript, Mr. Tapuskovic. Page 17, line 5 and 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. It says: "You can see that the photograph is a bit lopsided, as I took it in haste, trying not to linger in the area for too long." And then I think what was left out was, "Because -- I had to take shelter because I was afraid that I might be shot," or something like that. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell the Judges what is the building behind this very high building that -- this building of several storeys.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: This was the Marsal Tito barracks that had been abandoned. The Yugoslav People's Army left the barracks sometime in 1992, and I don't know what. Now it's been renovated to a certain extent. At any rate, this is the former Marsal Tito barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us, is this where the tram line passes, somewhere here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: On the opposite side, across from this building, down there beyond is where the tram line runs. I believe this is the tram stop between Pofalici and the museum. There is a tram stop somewhere there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me not correct the transcript, but what did you say the building opposite was like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I know when the building was made. On the lateral sides it has windows, and as -- and on this side that we see, well, the identical facade is on the opposite side. That's what the architectural layout of the building was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were not able to take photographs from that other side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: No. That wasn't possible at all. I would have to go across and then take a photograph of the building standing on the tram tracks in order to obtain exactly the same photograph as I've made.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we please have the photograph admitted as a Defence exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D324, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at page 91 of DD003335. Page 91.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, please look at photograph 131 -- or, rather, 181. A moment ago you said that you saw civilians that were shot. Is this photograph consistent with what you were talking about? What can you tell us about this photograph? Did you take it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes, I took this photograph. This woman was hit by sniper fire, and she's wounded to her leg, and you can see her leg bleeding. However, nobody dared approach her until a van arrived, because this area was under constant sniper fire, and nobody dared approach her before we had a vehicle to take her to the hospital. And then a van arrived, and we took the lady to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can this photograph be admitted, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let me hear Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, of course I don't object in principle. However, the quality is, in my submission, very poor, and I really can't see the evidential value for this photograph. Unless -- unless there are negatives or unless there's a colour photograph or -- and also, perhaps we can get, if he hasn't done already, a date of when this photograph was taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I have to agree the quality is very poor. It almost distorts the image of the lady.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have managed to produce a large number of photographs in -- of good quality, and I will provide you with a photograph in one or two days, and if this one could be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I also forgot to ask when the photograph was taken, what year and what month.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: This photograph was taken in August of 1994. I don't recall the exact date. I do know I happened to pass by on that day. I noticed this incident and photographed it. In this particular area of town quite a few people were shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the photograph be at least marked for identification? I have another similar one. I will also provide Their Honours with a good-quality copy of it this evening or tomorrow or in accordance with the Chamber's orders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Just to -- for counsel to ask the witness through Your Honour, the area of town that he's speaking about, I didn't quite get the location of the photograph, of where the photograph was taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Where was the photograph taken, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This photograph was taken at the beginning of the Zagrebacka street at Grbavica. I don't know the house number exactly, perhaps around house 40. As you head to Grbavica from Vrace, this is where Zagrebacka street is located. The lady was probably walking along the sidewalk and was probably unaware of the fact that a sniper was active there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mark it for identification pending the production of a better photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this will be marked for identification as D325.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will have the same request to make in relation to the following photograph. I will provide you with documents tomorrow. Document DD3335, page 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, let me not repeat all my questions in -- that I put to you in relation to the earlier photograph. Can you tell us what this photograph shows, who took it and when? This first photograph. I will also have questions for you in relation to the other photographs, but let this photograph be shown the way it was before.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: This photograph was taken sometime in October of 1994. I know that it was raining, and it was quite chilly. A woman was going to collect water, and she was shot from the faculty of mathematics, the building we just referred to. I believe that this street is Lenjinova street. She was walking between two buildings. She wasn't cautious enough or maybe she didn't know about the new hole that was made. She was shot. We couldn't approach her. She was there for some two days. They covered her with a nylon. I made quite a few photographs and they were of good quality. I don't know why this one is of such poor quality.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this photograph be admitted as a Defence exhibit? Can it be marked for identification, and then I will provide you with a good photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. This will be marked for identification as Exhibit D326.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spoke of snipers, gunfire. The buildings at Grbavica where you stayed at the time, were they also shot at from some other weapons or some other projectiles from different weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Almost throughout the time, even during cease-fires, some rifle-launched grenades that were handmade were shot, and the only purpose was to basically have the window-panes shattered and to have these grenade enter the town and set fire to the building. They were mostly shot from Sarajevo towards Grbavica. I was shown by some lads what they looked like, because they had managed to get hold of one of those that were defective and did not explode.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we look another photograph from DD3335, page 1, namely photograph number 3. Who took this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I took this photograph. The lads, the soldiers brought them to me to show them to me to see how these projectiles were made in Sarajevo. They told me that these were a rifle-launched grenade with a flammable charge. The primary objective is to have a flat set alight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can this photograph also be admitted into evidence, please, because I will show now the building out of which these projectiles were fired?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, now, I do object to the admission of this photograph. The witness has identified that a group of soldiers, we don't know which soldiers, brought these to him and said they came from -- what I think the witness is saying came from the ABiH weapons. I can't see -- I understand that hearsay is admissible but for me this is really tenuous evidence. And I can't see the relevance either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Not to be admitted, reliability is tenuous.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you said that such weapons were used to fire at flats and to set them alight, I will show you photograph DD003335, photograph number 63. Tell me, the weapons we looked at a moment ago and the damage we see on the building, is the damage in fact inflicted by such projectiles, the one we see here?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I -- I submit that there needs to be foundation for -- foundation laid for the witness to answer such question. In other words, how familiar is the witness with the kinds of rounds that may cause certain craters or certain holes. There needs to be some basic knowledge of ballistics or weaponry, and as this witness has testified, he was not in the military, he never wanted nor did he carry a weapon. So if Mr. Tapuskovic can establish a basis for the witness's knowledge, then of course, but at this stage, before answering the question, at least that needs to be, in my submission, established.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tapuskovic. Seek to lay a foundation for the witness to provide this evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness showed those contraptions used to fire at homes and set fire to them. That's what he said. And he said that many flats or apartments were set on fire by this kind of weapon, the only aim of which was to cause fires. This is a photograph the witness took, and let's first hear where this building was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, you have not carried out my instruction. Evidently you did not hear. You are to establish -- you are to establish a basis for the witness to give this kind of evidence. There is merit in the submission from the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know all this? How do you learn about it? I don't know how else to put this. What you said about people's homes being set on fire and about those kind of projectiles being launched, how did you know about all this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Some soldiers called me over and showed that to me. They told me to take the photograph. They said these were handmade rifle-launched grenades.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. That's what you told us. But you told us that homes were set on fire. Did you see with your own eyes those kind of projectiles doing this and people's flats burning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I saw that personally, and maybe we'll come across those photographs later. I saw flats on fire, and some of those projectiles failed to explode, and they were brought to me. They have something inside to start a fire. So the upper floors of buildings were fired at with those projectiles. And although I'm not a soldier, I came to understand what those projectiles were. The soldiers told me, "Look. These are rifle-launched grenades, the purpose of which is to set fire to flats." These were in addition to those industrially made rifle-launched grenades that they fired at Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Is this a building that suffered that fate?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. President, I still -- I still persist, because now the witness has said that the soldiers told him that these were the grenades that were fired on these flats and the witness has said that the soldiers told him of the purpose. In other words, the purpose to set alight these flats. So it's not only hearsay evidence in the extreme, but it's also opinion evidence by soldiers passed down to this witness, and this witness is now testifying about the purpose, through this very, very shaky link, in my submission. So I still can't see how the witness can answer these questions reliably.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We are not admitting this, Mr. Tapuskovic. Unless you have better evidence than this from the witness, just stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask him whether he saw this building burning?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No. I've already ruled on it. Now, move to your next piece of evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll come to other buildings, but now let's see what those screens looked like, the ones you said you had to erect to protect yourself from snipers. For example, let's look at DD004233. It's a good quality photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, what is the point of this? We have already seen screens used for that purpose by both sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I can stop asking questions about this. I have a few pictures which are very eloquent, showing what people had to do to protect themselves from gunfire, and I can ask where this is located, but all this shows --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... but only if it takes the evidence any further. I mean, to show the screens to protect themselves, doesn't take the matter any further. We've already seen that. And there's no doubt -- the Prosecution isn't doubting that Serbs had erect screens to protect themselves. I have no doubt that they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, then I'll ask you directly. You've shown those buildings. You've shown those two women who were killed -- or, rather, one was wounded, another was killed. How many persons like that were there that you know of who were killed or wounded by fire, whether infantry, sniper, and how many photographs could you have brought here had I asked you to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I have voluminous archives. There are many such instances. I selected these two and showed them to you and you said that was all right. I have a lot of that material from 1992 to 1995. There were many casualties. I know that there was one day where eight people were shot by snipers, fatally shot on one day and four others wounded, and that was on one day alone. Those persons were taken to the Kasindol hospital.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I have no doubt that all these photographs would be very appropriate for a museum, but their evidential value, Mr. Tapuskovic, is exceedingly questionable.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Their Honours say that it has already been shown that many civilians were killed or wounded. There were some photographs I wanted to show. Let's show at least one to show what persons had to resort to in order to tend to their gardens. I will show just that one photograph, and I will refrain from showing others I meant to show. So let's have just one if we may, just one of the photographs I wanted to show about this to show what a man living in such circumstances had to do in order to be able to tend to his garden, because we heard here about Serbs shooting at people digging in their gardens, going to funerals, and so on. So let's see what life was like for people on the other side. Let's show just one photograph, and if Your Honours feel it's not relevant, then of course I'll stop there, at least when it comes to these screens. By your leave, let me just show DD004273.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know why this is such poor quality. It's in excellent condition. If it could be placed on the ELMO. I don't understand why it looks like this here. Could it be placed on the ELMO? If the witness could explain where and when he took this photograph. I don't explain myself. Let the witness explain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain, Witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, explain.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This photograph was taken in the spring of 1995 in the Nedzarici neighbourhood. I don't know the name of the street. I noticed a man who was digging in his garden with a hoe, but in order to move around the area in front of his house he had to place these tin sheets to protect himself from sniper fire. He had a small garden round his house which he cultivated to grow food.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this photograph be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D327, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's time for the break. Do you have any more questions, Mr. Tapuskovic?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a short film of two minutes taken by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, we'll take the break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: In Judge Harhoff's absence, Judge Mindua and I sit pursuant to Rule 15 bis. Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can we explain to the Judges the following: It has been stated here that you do not know anything about weapons. Is that right? Please explain to the Judges that you held certain duties with what unit exactly, and did you also have some military duties to perform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I was at the press centre attached to the corps command. I did not take part in combat. That's the only thing I did not participate in, but otherwise I was a conscript.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say you were at the press centre. What were your duties exactly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I was charged with going to various sites and taking photographs. I took foreign crews there, and wherever I went I was explained what had been going on. I came to learn a great deal of things and to know what sort of weapons were used where.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to send all the information you had, including the photographs, to the mass media that had nothing to do with the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: There were such cases. We allowed for the material to be taken and publicised. It all depended on the crews that came, on the mass media involved. Some of them used the material, others were simply not interested in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did representatives of foreign television and media companies show any interest in the material you had and was any of it publicised?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I followed the broadcasts of various mass media, and I observed that some of the crews had used the material we provided. Others were simply not interested. The material was used by them in the manner they wished. Sometimes we would note that the material had been used in the ways that we did not deem favourable. However, we provided our material to all those who expressed -- to such crews as expressed interest in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Since you moved about in the field, can you tell us whether you were able to see where the lines of separation were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I was familiar with the lines of separation for the most part. Very often I had to ask someone who was well -- who was familiar with the situation, who was well-versed in the situation to escort me to the front line so would I not come in harm's way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Since you lived at Grbavica, are you quite familiar with the situation there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I was quite familiar with the situation at Grbavica. If I was on the move, I simply had to adhere to the rules that we had concerning sniper fire. I had to consult with people, where the places were, where one had to accelerate movement, because as I said, there were victims from sniper fire. This happened on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please tell me what was the geographical position of Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: This is a part of the urban part of Sarajevo on the left bank of the Miljacka. On the right bank of the Miljacka there were high-rise buildings under the control of the BH army. On one side Grbavica was at risk from Mojmilo, from Asimovo Brdo, Sanac. That's close to the Zeleznica football team stadium. They were up there above that area on the hilltop. We were quite afraid of the hill, and we were very cautious.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Was there another hill as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: We called it Debelo Brdo. Sometime in the autumn of 1994, the BH army doing out a trench and came up on the hilltop. The hill overlooks Grbavica, and one can clearly see the Lukavica-Pale road from it. There, in the immediate vicinity of the hill, there was an UNPROFOR check-point, and they --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I will show you photograph DD004226.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the quality of this photograph is quite poor. Perhaps we should place the photograph on the ELMO so as not to have my learned friend Sachdeva complaining about the quality of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, who took this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I took this photograph, and I believe it was in the autumn of 1994. I was taking this photograph from the direction of Grbavica, from a building that provided this view. I can indicate on this photograph if you want me to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Pause there, please. Tell us first what the photograph shows?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: This is called Debelo Brdo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were the positions of the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Perhaps I can draw them on the photograph here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: What you see down here is the end of the Jewish cemetery or, rather, the top-most part of it, and this is roughly where the lines were. What you see down there is the Kovacici or Donje Kovacici neighbourhood as they call it. It was under the control of --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please mark the line you drew with the letter "S".

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you please mark the Kovacici neighbourhood with a capital letter "K".

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the circle you made, what was there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: That's the line of separation at the Jewish cemetery. This is the edge of the Jewish cemetery, which was practically under the control of the Bosnian army rather than anyone else's.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who held the hill at the time you took the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: You can see the trench here that was dug by members of the BH army. You can see how it stretches upwards all the way down to this -- all the way up to this place where you could have a clear view of the Lukavica-Pale road or Grbavica-Pale road and control it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you draw an arrow pointing in that direction.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And mark it with the letter "M".

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is Zlatiste exactly? Can you explain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: You can see a part of it in this area there, a part of the Zlatiste fort.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please mark it with a "Z", please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there soldiers there of any side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: No, there were no soldiers there at all. This was a ruin that was not easily accessible and one exposed oneself to great risk if one attempted to go there. There was a lot of shrubbery and forest there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now that we're talking about Zlatiste, can you draw us the line indicating where the road ran?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: There, behind this forest there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you mark it with the letter "O", please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It stretched further on toward Pale.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes, to the left toward Pale, to the right toward Lukavica -- or, rather, Grbavica. And at one point at this site that I marked, one could clearly see the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see the BH army firing from this hilltop in the direction of the road towards Zlatiste?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I was present on several occasions when there were ongoing activities. On the first occasion I was told that they were firing upon Vrace and a house was set on fire there. I even brought a photograph to that effect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us -- or, rather, draw a line, an arrow indicating the direction of the combat activities.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Toward Grbavica and Vrace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but what about Zlatiste? What about the road at Zlatiste? What was the direction of the activities there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: You see the arrow marked "M" behind the hilltop as the road bent, you could see at least half a kilometre of the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did -- was there any fire upon this line up there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes, there was. It was quite risky to take that road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please draw an arrow indicating the direction of fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Not only from this vantage point but also from this area here as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please mark the left marking with the letter "L" and the right marking, the right arrow, with the letter "F".

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we have this photograph admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D328, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at photograph DD00-4230, since you mentioned the road across Zlatiste. The first one. It's not good enough. Could we place the photograph I have on the ELMO. A moment ago you mentioned Zlatiste. Has this photograph anything to do with Zlatiste?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: This photograph was taken along the Lukavica-Pale road just -- just above the settlement called Zlatiste. You can see here that the screen on the roadside was damaged, because oftentimes they would fire a rifle-launched grenade at this screen wherever they felt that somebody was taking the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please draw an arrow indicating the direction from which the grenade arrived and where it impacted.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any casualties involved?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I know for a fact that on the 17th of June a man was killed shortly before the photograph was taken. A grenade impacted against this concrete wall and the man was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the man heading?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Towards Pale.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he walking in just the same way as the two persons we see on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes. When one took this road one had to be quiet, because as soon as they heard a human voice they fired a grenade or some other projectile. And one never took this road unless one really needed to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you draw a line -- you said that this -- that the person was moving in the direction of Pale. Can you draw a line to that effect and mark it with the letter "P".

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What followed there behind the bend we can see here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Beyond the bend there was an observation post of the army of the Republika Srpska. I believe it was in mid-May that General Milosevic was wounded there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can this photograph be admitted as a Defence exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D329, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you say? When was this photograph taken? Did I understand you correctly when you -- or, rather, I will not speak on the matter. Tell us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: This was taken on the 17th of June, 1995. Sometime before that date, I believe it was in mid-May, that General Milosevic was wounded on this spot at that forward post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know the date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: No. I only heard that he was wounded. I didn't know any details surrounding that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said -- or, rather, has this photograph been assigned a number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. That was admitted as D329.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any fire from Mojmilo upon Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: One part of Grbavica lay beneath Mojmilo or, rather, beneath the Zeleznica football club stadium. This was held by the BH army. We were constantly exposed to dangers from that area. That area was called Sanac but is in fact part of Mojmilo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me show you DD004240. It's a photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is a poor copy too. I have a better one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judges what this is? You've just indicated that there was Sanac and Mojmilo. What is this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: This is part of Mojmilo, whereas this specific area here is called Sanac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please circle it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Place the letter "S" with a diacritic "Sh" in the middle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was positioned there? Which army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Members of the BH army were there. Right beneath there lies Grbavica. You can see one of the flashlights of the Zeleznica football club stadium. Beneath the floodlights there, you have Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please the letter "G" there, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who held the position along the top of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: All these oppositions of the Bosnian army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please draw a line.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mark it with the letter "B".

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this where shots were fired on Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes. There was fire coming from there on Grbavica, and also from this part of the of hill there was fire towards Lukavica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Draw an arrow in that direction, and mark it with the letter L.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wish to tender this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D330, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I now wish to show you a similar photograph, and please tell us when it was taken and what it shows. It's DD004241. Could we again put this on the ELMO, please. Can you tell us when this photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: This photograph was taken in 1995, and here one can see part of Asim's hill. Asimovo Brdo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please whenever you indicate something, circle it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: This is Sanac, Asimovo Brdo, Asim's hill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is this here that's burning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: That's a building at Grbavica. It was set alight from up above with those improvised projectiles. I even came here with some soldiers, and in one apartment or flat I saw an unexploded improvised rifle-launched grenade. And then the soldiers brought me more of those and I took that photograph. I took at that photograph that you saw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what time was this taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Around June or July 1995, I think. I had a lot of those photographs, so it's hard to be precise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And who was holding the positions along the top of the hill? If you know who was holding those positions draw a line, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: All along this line were positions of the Bosnian army up until the end of Mojmilo, the waterworks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mark it with a "B".

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wish to tender this photograph as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D331, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course you took all these photographs yourself with your own camera.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes. I took all of those photographs, and I remember taking them. I had to do everything in black and white because I didn't have any colour film. It was very hard to come by photographic material. Some foreign teams would leave me a roll or two of film.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I now wish to show you DD004224.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again the quality is bad. Could we place this on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what this photograph shows? What hill is that over there? What hill is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: The hill with the point on it is the hill of Hum.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mark it, please. Mark everything you say. With an "H".

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what made these holes here, do you know? What is this, first of all. Can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: This is the Vrace memorial park where during World War II patriots were shot, Jews also, Serbs, and all patriots. And this park, memorial park, was shot at with a recoilless gun. You can see the rubble that has fallen inside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From what direction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: From Hum. And also the clinic at Vrace was targeted with a recoilless gun because they told me that a recoilless gun causes this kind of damage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you draw a line to indicate from where the fire came.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mark it with a "A".

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wish to tender this also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D332, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know something about fire from the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina when it comes to Mount Igman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Well, they kept firing from Igman. Ilidza was under threat, as well as a neighbourhood called Vojkovici. The army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was at Igman, and those places were very close to the line, and on more than one occasion I saw the consequences of that firing from Igman on Vojkovici and Ilidza.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd now like to show you DD004244. Again the quality is poor. When you spoke about the consequences of fire from Igman, does it have anything to do with this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: This photograph is directly connected to that. You can see the remains of a house. It was an old house built of brick, and these are the top -- this is the top of Mount Igman. And when I was here, they told me that this house had been destroyed, and I think two people were killed, and they said it was something called a "fagot". I really don't understand about these weapons, but this house was reduced to this condition that we see here. It's below Igman towards Stojcevac on territory held by members of the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please mark that first line with the letter "I".

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that was the top of Mount Igman or, rather, the ridge of Mount Igman and the rubble of that house with "S" and the direction from which that projectile might have come?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Well, from the middle part of Igman, they came down towards Ilidza and the source of the River Bosna and I know that an APC was hit on the crossroads near the Drin [phoen] bridge, as they called it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you say this place was called which was under the control of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: This was below Igman. It's a part of Ilidza towards Stojcevac. I don't know what the village is called or, rather, the neighbourhood but it's near Hrasnica, and very close to these houses there were other lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wish to tender this photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D333, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you spoke about fire coming from the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. What did the houses in Grbavica, Nedzarici, Dobrinja and other areas look like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Well, in these places houses were destroyed, damaged especially in 1994 or 1995, on two or three occasions something was always happening. Although, I know there were lulls in the fighting but reports kept coming that the Bosniak side was digging trenches in this direction and that direction, breaking through walls between buildings and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would now like to show you two photographs. One is important because of very important circumstances here, but first let's see DD004272.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again we have the same problem. I apologise for having to get you up every so often.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this what you were talking about? And where is this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: These are houses in Nedzarici. The army of Republika Srpska was here. In the basement of these houses there was an elderly man who was living there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I tender this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D334, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps the witness can explain on what basis he knows an elderly man was living there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I don't think that's necessary. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's show one more building that was mentioned here very often, DD004255.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, again the same problem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, what building is this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: This is the Metalka building on the bank of the Miljacka near the Vrbanja bridge. That's what it was called then. And I know that in 1992 a woman was killed in this building, and this building was very dangerous to approach, especially the entrances. I think in 1994 and 1995 nobody lived here. Nobody could approach that side. And on the right-hand side here there was a UN check-point, two large dugouts, right next to the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: 1994, 1995. This photograph I know was taken, in fact, in 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, what does this photograph, for example, show that is of value to the case?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What can we see on this photograph? What building is this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, I'm asking you, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness said that in 1994, 1995 -- Your Honours, it shows, first of all, that there was constant fighting and that this building was fired on by the artillery of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. It's the Metalka building, and the witness says that at that time there was nobody there because no one could live in it, first of all. And secondly, nearby were UNPROFOR check-points in 1994 and 1995. The witness stated this. And all this is in the context of constant fighting. This building was constantly under fire, as were other buildings. I can show you hundreds of photographs. I've shown only a few which are important for this case. I could show you a thousand photographs perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. To what effect? That's the question. Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, firstly, I fail to see how a photograph taken on a particular day demonstrates that there was constant fighting or that this building was constantly targeted. The photograph does not, in my submission, demonstrate that. And so for counsel to suggest that, is, in my submission, incorrect. And again, I -- I do not see -- I do not see the relevance of -- of this photograph to the case and to the charges against the accused. So I would object to the admission of this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Sachdeva, we have some -- we have evidence in the case of course that the Metalka building was significant. There was firing from it, and it was fired upon. The -- we'll -- we'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D335, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Okay. You have exhausted your time now, Mr. Tapuskovic. I have just been told by the court deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will try to finish quite soon. Quite correctly at the outset we were cautioned about the relevance of showing some documents material to the witness. However, the presentation of the photographs to the witness takes quite a long time. Can I please have some additional time? I will soon finish. I still have video footage of two minutes that I have to show the witness, and I'll try to go through that quite fast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Then let's proceed as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I have to go back to some other issues we have talked about, the photographs, and what they depicted. You said that you knew that Dragomir Milosevic had taken up the command position in the month of August. What was situation like in those early days of General Milosevic becoming the commander, and did you ever come across him when you -- as you worked in the press office?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I would come across General Milosevic quite often at the press office building whenever I was on my way out or on my way in. At that point in time there was some sort of a cease-fire in force. There was not much gunfire. I keep repeating that the Bosniak side was digging trenches and advancing toward our forces, even toward the UNPROFOR, and I believe all of this is documented. I recall that since there was a cease-fire on, I was even off duty for a while as I had some family matters I had to attend to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you sent out for an assignment in the month of October?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes, I was assigned to go to Cakle. Even the French UN contingent drove me up there to Cakle. This is beyond Igman and Treskavica. I was to go there because an incident had occurred. I know that was protected zone that had been demilitarised. There should not have been any combat activities there. There was the headquarters of the Medical Corps and the logistics of a battalion of the 2nd Sarajevo Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened in the demilitarised zone there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: This came as a shock to all of us. Allegedly there was a cease-fire, and the French soldiers were surprised. They organised a team. They put a team together to carry out an on-site investigation up there and to take photographs. We simply could not believe that a sabotage group could launch a raid against the headquarters there. I took photographs. Twelve persons were killed. I know that a nurse by the name of Bjelica was killed. I recall her in particular because her brother had been killed in the war, and her father came over there later on. This was taken as serious incident. The French joined us -- or, rather, took us up there and carried out an on-site investigation, which shows how seriously they took it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I could also show you a photograph depicting UNPROFOR, will you bet me show you DD004261 first.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I suppose we'd better put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are these the bodies of the soldiers killed in the demilitarised zone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes. This was taken at the scene. Everything had been left untouched for the French to come in and see the scene. This is the start of the compound, and up there in the forest the raid was launched. There were some charred bodies there, and here in the foreground there were bodies of the people who were trying to flee the area. Among them was the nurse who was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I tender this photograph into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object on the grounds of relevance. This photograph depicts soldiers, deceased soldiers and deceased soldiers take place in -- soldiers get killed in war, and I can't see how this, in my submission, furthers -- would assist you in determining matters in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, what is the relevance of this? You've heard the objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was a very important moment in the conflict. Very important key witnesses of the Prosecution testified about this. Among them, protected witness W-46, not to mention others. Several witnesses therefore spoke to this event in the demilitarised zone and about how it had an impact on the overall situation and the warring parties. This was an important event, testifying about the violation of the demilitarised zone, which led to the loss of a great many lives, including nurses. A column had been attacked which also included nurses. This is an important event which had to do with several other matters, and among others Witness W-46 testified about this. This photograph is, among other things, also a confirmation of that testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I can't be 100 per cent sure, but I am, as much as I can be, that the evidence that learned counsel is speaking to must have come out of cross-examination. It certainly was not part of the Prosecution case in chief. And in addition, the photograph does not -- the photograph is of soldiers. It depicts soldiers and not -- not nurses. So I still can't see how this assists -- assists Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We will admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D336, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since my learned friend Sachdeva says that there wasn't a nurse there, I want the to call up DD004262, which is a photograph depicting that young lady who was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this the nurse?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes. This is the nurse. I know that her family name is Bjelica. She was found a bit further down, further away from the soldiers as she was trying to get away.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
