utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have this photograph admitted as a Defence exhibit? This shows that even a nurse was killed in an action launched against a demilitarised zone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D337, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am nearing the end of my examination.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you said that you knew that in mid-June of 1995, General Milosevic was wounded.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes. I know. I know that he was wounded at an observation post. I did not come across the general in that period of time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know when he went away on sick leave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I believe it was sometime in August of 1995. Sometime in that period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you base your answer on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I know that I heard them talking about the general having to go on sick leave, and he was simply not there in that period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have a request to make. When his driver was testifying, at that time we did not have the translation of the medical documentation from the hospital where General Dragomir Milosevic was treated. This witness has confirmed to you now that he knew he had been wounded and that he had been away for a while. Therefore, this medical documentation which has now been translated and which shows that for a while he was absent, as had been confirmed by other witnesses, he had been away from the positions since he was in the hospital, I would like this medical document to be admitted. This is DD003 -- or, rather, 1089.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter isn't sure about the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: What is it? What is the document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's not clear to me how this witness is going to speak to the medical document, to the information on it. You can try. Let us see whether the witness knows anything about the information on it. Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Well, I'll wait, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this witness has confirmed, and there were other witnesses, several witnesses had been examined about this matter, including his driver, who drove him for his treatment to Belgrade in early August. He returned, as other witnesses testified, in early September. At that time when that witness was being examined the medical documentation had not been translated as yet. This was something you observed. In the meantime, the service here has translated the documentation. This witness here knows that the general was absent in the month of August and that he was away for treatment. This medical documentation -- rather, we will have a medical expert witness who will be able to comment on it. This is the letter of discharge which shows that he was in the hospital from the 9th of August until the 1st of September and that later on he was on sick leave at home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How am I to admit it? You haven't asked the witness a single question about the document. You're seeking to have it admitted through this witness. So he has to be able to speak to the contents of the certificate, and you haven't asked him a single question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct. I've run ahead of myself. I've started from the end rather than from the beginning. But very well. This is DD003189. Page 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While we're waiting for the document to appear, you say that you used to see him. When you were working at the press service, where were you exactly located in the building in relation to where the accused was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: The press service was on the ground floor of the building next to the entrance, and upstairs were the offices of General Milosevic. If I happened to be at the press service as his escort, the lads who were with him would come over to me and we could chat. And I know that they told me that General Milosevic was supposed to go away for treatment, that he would be absent because he had problems with his health. And I believe that this was in early August of 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Here is the document. Can we show the letter of discharge, which is page 3. This is page -- or, rather, page 5 of the B/C/S. The page immediately before this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, now I -- with respect, I don't see how, especially after Mr. Tapuskovic himself has said that he has started at the end and not at the beginning, in other words, essentially given evidence from the bar table, and now he's asking the witness certain questions which -- which in my submission has already been -- the answers have already been aired in court. And secondly, the witness, if one peruses the evidence thus far, even the witness has given contradictory evidence as to the date of wounding of General Milosevic which I obviously will bring out in cross-examination or I don't need to, but since it relates to this -- since on that basis this document is being put to the witness, I don't see how the witness can give reliable answers on the document. The Prosecution does not object to the admission of the document, but not through this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: All right. Continue. We'll decide on the question of its admission, if you're going to seek its admission, at the end of the witness's evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we see that two minutes of footage which has to do with everything the witness has said so far? It's only two minutes long, and then Your Honours will see whether it's significant or not in the context of what the witness has already spoken about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You've said it's two minutes. Let's see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who made this film, sir? Witness, who made this film?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I made this film sometime in May -- or, rather, in the spring. It was a rainy day of 1995. I was at Pale, and I set out from Pale with a crew, and I made the video along the way. It's the road leading from Pale to Grbavica. And in certain places you can see those protective screens made of boards to protect from snipers and other fire, and when you go from Grbavica to Vrace you can see more protection to -- to avoid buses by being seen. And then in order to be safe you have to go -- and then when you go to Grbavica towards the town, you see all those curtains hanging. And it was there because without that you simply couldn't get through.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the name of the street leading down towards Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: It used to be called Zagrebacka Street, and then Rave Jankovica continues along it. It's actually going from Vrace to Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how far from that street were BH army positions? I'm referring to Mojmilo and Debelo Brdo.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I can't be precise, but from Debelo Brdo it was quite close. I don't know if it's as much as a kilometre, a thousand metres as the crow flies, and on the other side, across the Miljacka, that street was completely exposed without those curtains that were set up for protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I wish to tender this footage which faithfully represents what the witness has described more than once with respect to those curtains protecting vehicles, civilians, people. It's the street mentioned by all the witnesses where there were the most casualties, and several Defence witnesses have spoken about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D338, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have completed my examination-in-chief. Thank you. Just a moment, please. There was a document which I haven't tendered with the first and last name of this witness. Our number was DD003984. Under seal. It has not been admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D339 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva, cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness T-41. My name is Manoj Sachdeva, and I'm a lawyer for the Prosecution and I'm going to ask you some questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: May I ask the court usher to -- oh, thank you very much. To lower the ELMO. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise, Your Honours. You said you would decide about this medical document at the end of today. I had tendered it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: At the end of the witness's evidence. That is after cross-examination and perhaps if there is re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, just going back to that video we just saw, when -- when it was being played you could hear some talking from the car, I take it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes. There was a conversation in the car. There was some foreigners, I think they were journalists, and their interpreter was explaining to them where we were going, what was happening, and giving the driver instructions, telling him where to watch out. I don't speak English, so I don't know, but later on when I saw the footage I explained where we were going and what was happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Well, you say later on when you saw the footage. Can I just clarify, were you in the car taking the footage at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes, I was in the car. I was sitting in front next to the driver. You can see this was taken while the car was driving. I know it was spring, and it was raining.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And when you say it was spring -- you said it was spring 1995. Can you recall, was it April or May, 1995? What month was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: This was in May, towards the end of May, I think, in 1995. I might have been able to find the precise date. I didn't try. Some journalists came along. I went with them from Pale to Lukavica. I sat in the front so I could film this. I think it was in late May, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So even though we understand the weather in Bosnia-Herzegovina, when you say it was towards the end of May it was essentially in the summer of 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Well, I know that in Sarajevo at the end of May the trees start budding. The first leaves appear on the trees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand the question. How can May be summer? How can May be said to be summer?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let us move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And, sir, that drive that you took, you said you were going from Pale to -- to Grbavica; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And were the journalists in the car, were they with you for the whole of that trip from Pale to Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I don't know what the place was called exactly. They came by and I got in the car with them, and I went up to Grbavica. And I had my camera on not all the time but almost all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And the clip that we saw, it ran for about two minutes, and you would agree with me that in that clip one could not make out or one could not hear the sound of gunfire or -- or shelling, could one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I don't remember. I didn't hear that. But I know that it's a risky road and that you had to keep to some rules. Drive on the left, speed up in certain spots, and so on. Probably had they seen us, they would have shot at us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: In any case that clip, you would agree with me it appeared to be a relaxed drive, did it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Well, I don't know who would be relaxed. Perhaps those people who were sitting in the car not knowing where they were going. But I wasn't relaxed. I had my camera on. I knew I was in constant danger on that road.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: During the trip from -- from Pale to Grbavica the car was not hit, was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: No, it wasn't hit, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If I could now ask for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How long did the trip last? Witness, how long was the trip?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't really say. I filmed two or three minutes. The drive from Trebevic triangle, I came in another car and then I went down to those guys and then they picked me up. They -- I got in the car with them, and then the place is called Prvi Sumar to Grbavica. How long the drive takes, I don't know. You saw that the road is narrow. It was in poor condition. It was very hard to move along that road.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, can we -- can we take it that it was over -- at least over one hour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: No, not even half an hour, because from Prvi Sumar we got down quite quickly. They had a very good car, those foreigners, and in some places we had to drive very fast to avoid coming under fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Incidentally, do you recall where these foreigners were from? Which media company were they from, since you were in the car with them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I know there was a TV crew from Belgrade, and they brought along some Englishmen, but who or what they were or what agency they worked for I don't know because I didn't stay with them. After Grbavica, half an hour later I went to my home to have lunch.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So they were from Belgrade. So presumably they were Serbian; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I know that the driver was probably a Serb. I didn't question him. But the others, there were four of us in the car, I think, the others were English.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Let me just try and get some clarification. I asked you about the media company. You said -- you said it was a TV crew from Belgrade. So is my understanding that the TV company from Belgrade brought along English journalists, and it was eventually for the -- well, is that the correct understanding?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I didn't say that the TV crew was from Belgrade but that some people from Belgrade brought I think in two cars a kind of TV crew or delegation from England.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Well, let me just try and clarify now, because your answer -- when I asked you the question, incidentally do you know where these foreigners were from? What media company were they from since you were in the car with them. Your answer was, "I know there was a TV crew from Belgrade and they brought along some Englishmen." So as you were in the car, can you just clarify to the Court was this indeed a TV crew -- was there a TV crew from Belgrade in the car?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I did not hear the witness speak of a TV crew from Belgrade. What I heard was there was some people or something like that. He didn't mention any TV crew from Belgrade. Can we see where that is?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, in 57, line 12. It just went off the screen. He said there was a TV crew from Belgrade. This is what is on the transcript at any rate. Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So, Witness, please just answer the question. Was there a TV crew from Belgrade with you, accompanying you, on at that drive, irrespective of whether there were English journalists there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: That was not a crew of a TV station from Serbia or Belgrade, but those journalists who came first got escorts in Belgrade to bring them to us, and what I said was a TV crew from Belgrade, but what I meant to say was Englishmen, because for me those Englishmen and those people from Belgrade were all a TV crew whom I was taking round the battlefields and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: What was the name of the -- what was the name of the company? What was the name of the media company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I don't know exactly now. I wasn't really paying attention to that at the time. The important thing for me was to reach to Lukavica or, rather, Grbavica. And since one of them was the person from Belgrade who was leading that crew, and nobody had told me that I needed to escort them around, I merely wanted to get a lift with them to Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: What was the name of the person who was leading the crew from Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I don't know the name of the man. I know the name of the man who received the crew and who took them around Grbavica. That's what I can tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, now I'm going to --

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I'd like photograph 3 -- D328 to be brought up, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: T-41, you remember marking this photograph, don't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And the area where you've marked it with a "Z", that area was controlled by the VRS, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes, it was. But nobody dared access the area or let alone linger there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If you could just please answer the question we can move quickly. Now, the -- you see the mountains just above the figure -- the letter "Z"? You see that hill there, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes, I do, if you're referring to this. This here and this here, if that's what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes. And the hills that you've just pointed to, they are -- they comprised part of Mount Trebevic, don't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: These are practically the hilltops of Mount Trebevic which are quite bare, and just beneath them the Lukavica-Pale road ran, which is the road across Zlatiste that was under constant threat.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And Mount Trebevic is higher in elevation than Debelo Brdo, is it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: It is, but Debelo Brdo is not clearly visible because of these foothills of Mount Trebevic and the forest. That's the only answer I can give you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not actually asking as to the visibility. I just simply want you to confirm that Mount Trebevic is higher in elevation to Debelo Brdo, and you agree with that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, in this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute, Mr. Sachdeva. We have to take the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, what is the position with -- I'll raise the matter with you at the end of the witness's evidence. Mr. Sachdeva, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness T-41, just before we had break I asked you about the hills, the Mount Trebevic hills, and in one of your answers you said yes -- you said -- sorry, you said, "These are practically the hilltops of Mount Trebevic, which are quite bare and just beneath them, the Lukavica-Pale road ran, which is the road across Zlatiste that was under constant threat." You remember that answer, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I can't see the text on the screen, which means I can't know whether I'm supposed to start or not. I know that there was -- this road was under constant threat. You can see the UN flag here. Fire would be opened upon this Lukavica-Pale road. I know as I was using the road on several occasions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. As I understand it, you are simply being asked to confirm that you said that these are practically the hilltops of Mount Trebevic and that they are quite bare and right beneath this is the Lukavica-Pale road, and there was a constant threat. You did say that. That's all you're being asked to do, not to go over the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And that road, that was the road that you were travelling on in this video that we saw just a moment ago, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes. A section of the road was filmed. I didn't film all of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes. Now, on this photograph, the photograph is still there, I would just like you to put a "T" to mark the photograph with a -- oh, yes. That could be a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sir, if you could just place the letter "T" on the -- on the slopes of Mount Trebevic, on the photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And on the other side, on the right-hand side, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And -- and if you could, sir, in the area where you had written "Z", if you could just put the letters "VRS" beside it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you said that the -- the Lukavica-Pale road was fired upon from Mojmilo. You remember saying that, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I don't recall saying that fire was opened upon this area from Mojmilo, but that other area beneath Vrace as you go down into the valley, that is where several sections of the road could be seen from Mojmilo. I even brought some of the photographs along to that effect. And this was certainly targeted. There were UNPROFOR bunkers and observation posts there. Whenever there was fighting going on one could -- one dared not move along that road. It was unsafe also for ambulances and such medical vehicles. They were forced to place some tubes there for protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sir, how did you know the fire came from that direction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Simply because a part of Grbavica -- or, rather, Vrace, Gornja Petrovacka street, I know that several flats were set alight there. As one passed the gate and the park towards Zlatiste, one could see that position, the newly dug bunker that they used to fire from.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So, sir, are you saying because there were ABiH positions there, the fire came from that direction? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: That's what I'm saying, and I'm certain of that. I'm certain that fire was opened from this spot upon Vrace, upon Gornja Petrovacka street, and a part of the road from the Vrace memorial park towards Zlatiste.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: You're certain because -- because it was common knowledge, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Not only because of that. On several occasions I was supposed to go to Pale or somewhere else toward Trebevic, and traffic was stopped. They had even pulled out an old damaged vehicle that had come under an attack there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I tender this. Before I do that, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sir, if you see on the left-hand side of the photograph, you'll see a building with a flag. Do you see that there, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do. I see the flag.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And that is the UNPROFOR position, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes. This is the location where, as of 1993, the United Nations forces were stationed at even before the trenches were dug out. Even though the UN forces were there, despite that, fire was opened upon the areas I indicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sir. Sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I even believe that this was indicated in one of the UN reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sir, please just try and answer the question as precisely as possible, otherwise we are not going to finish tonight, and if there is another information I would like to get from you, I will ask those questions. Now, I would like you to please just put the letters "UN" on top of that or close to that building with the flag, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And, Mr. President, I tender that photograph into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P908, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If I could now ask for the marked photograph of Defence Exhibit 329 to be shown to the witness. And, Mr. President, may I ask your leave to have the Court usher just show me the hard copy, because the hard copy, it appears clearer in the hard copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic. No?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sir, this is the -- this is the Lukavica-Pale road, is it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes, this is the Lukavica-Pale road.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And it's correct, firstly, isn't it, if you look closely at the figures that are walking there, they are carrying rifles, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I think they are. On that day I was going up there, and there were some soldiers who were heading I don't know where. The point was that we had to be very, very quiet as we were moving in order to avoid being shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sir, I simply again asked if they were carrying rifles, and you have confirmed that they were carrying rifles. And they -- let me ask you this: They --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I conferred with my colleague. It doesn't have anything to do with what was just said now. It has to do with the photograph from earlier on. We are not sure whether our photograph in the condition in which it was before the Prosecutor placed markings on it has been saved, or whether the markings that were made during my examination and the photograph with those markings no longer exists. I suppose the Prosecutor should use a different photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If I may, ideally each party would use separate exhibit if they were going to direct the witness to mark on it. However, as a work-around we could have separate colours, the Defence markings in blue, OTP markings in red, and the metadata will reflect this, as well as the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very good. Yes, Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, sir, you said shortly before the photograph you took was taken a man was killed on this road. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And you said that the man was killed on the 17th of June, and I understand it's 1995; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I believe that that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And you also said, however, that the photograph was taken on the 17th of June. So may I ask, did you take this photograph on the day that the man died?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes. I took the photograph on at that day. The man was killed shortly before. I didn't see that. We were told that a man had been killed and we should be very cautious as we were moving along the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you know who the person was that was killed, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I don't know. I do know that from -- that he was from a neighbourhood close by. The village is called Petrovic, and I know he was buried somewhere there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And you, of course, weren't there when -- when he was killed, were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: No, I wasn't there at that moment when he was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And you said that a grenade had impacted on the concrete wall. Where on the concrete wall did the grenade impact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. Roughly where the arrow is placed. It was a rifle-launched grenade which normally bursts into fragments, and that's what killed the man.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: You -- we really can't see any holes in the wall, can we, any markings from the fragments in the wall on this photograph, can we, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Well, I don't know how come you can't see them, but look. Beyond this rock you see that the wall is damaged. This rifle-launched grenade wouldn't leave much of a hole in the wall. It bursts into shrapnel. Of perhaps even this damage on the concrete wall comes from that projectile, but I did not give it much thought. I did not try and observe the wall for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: The point is, sir, that you weren't there when this man was killed, so you don't -- you don't know -- you don't know, firstly, that it was indeed a rifle-launched grenade, and you don't know where it came from, do you, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I did not observe the grenade as it was flying. I wasn't able to. I was going toward Trebevic with these men, and we were cautioned that we should move silently above all, as perhaps in half an hour earlier a man from Petrovic had been killed there. I know that the following day this person from Petrovic was buried. I did not personally observe that event. I was merely cautioned by persons who were passing that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So your evidence about it -- about it being a rifle-launched grenade is pure speculation, isn't it, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean. If a person who is passing by who is a soldier, I don't know what, and if he tells me that they are launching rifle grenades and that they cannot be heard and that we should move silently, so they do not observe us, well ...

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And are you saying, sir, that the rifle grenade came over the fence in the manner in which you've drawn this arrow, sir, in that arc fashion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I don't know what the arch was. I know that the BH army positions are quite close down there, and I know that if someone is observed passing there that rifle grenades are launched at them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And you said the ABiH positions -- you said the ABiH positions are quite close down there. Presumably you're saying that ABiH positions were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Several times, Your Honours, it was said that they were cautioned and that they were told that they are listening, the enemy side is listening whether somebody is passing by over there and that they should pass silently through that area. This wasn't entered in the transcript, that they were told the movement across the road was heard which prompts an action, but this wasn't reflected in the transcript. That they should move cautiously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I do recall something to that effect. I can't say whether it was exactly as you have just put it. Let us move on, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sir, I just want to confirm that you -- you said that the ABiH positions were quite close down there, and so I take it that the ABiH positions were -- where you say the fire came from were down from this road; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: The BH army positions were behind the wall down there. At Trebevic, in that part, there is a plateau of sorts, and this is a forested area, and given the range of a rifle grenade, this is quite close and it was quite risky to pass through there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sir, I'm just trying to establish that. You keep saying that the ABiH positions were down there. So my question to you is that the positions were -- in terms of height they were lower down from this road, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: On this side, behind the fence, there is a small slope and then a plateau where the positions of the BH army were.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So they were lower than the road, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes, they were lower, but not a great deal lower. The slope is quite gentle there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And a rifle grenade is a direct fire weapon, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I don't know that. All I know is that they launched across the protective fence as soon as they hear someone passing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, when I asked the witness about certain features of weapons my learned friend Sachdeva objected to that and on the basis of the witness not knowing anything about the weapons. So now the witness should not be asked to explain what a rifle-launched grenade is. I wasn't able to clarify some matters with the witness which had to do with the photographs he had taken. Therefore, I believe we should adhere to the same rule in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, might I respond?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: The witness has repeatedly now in evidence in chief and in cross-examination stated that rifle grenades were launched and -- and therefore I submit I'm entitled to cross-examine on that knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, Witness, if I could now move to the -- the next photograph. That's D3 -- I want to show you D332. Witness -- sorry, Witness, before I start asking you questions on this photograph, I just want to take you back to the 17th of June, the day that you took that previous photograph and the day that you said a man was killed. You understand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And I take it that when you went to take the photograph -- well, how long -- how long did you spend on that road, on the scene, when you were taking the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I reached just ahead of this site by car. The men, the people who were there, explained to us that we should not stay there for long, that we should make sure that we make no noise and that we should try and avoid this place as we are moving along the road, to the sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And I take it that to take the photograph you got out of the car and took the photograph; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes. The car stayed further down. We practically had to scurry along this stretch of the road that you can see, and then the driver in the car joined us. He speeded up on this section of the road, picked us up and then went on. We did not dare to reach this spot by car because the engine would be heard easily, and we could not allow that to happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: How many cars were in this convoy or was it just one car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: There was just this one car. In those days one did not take this road unless it was strictly necessary, and then one had to assume the risk it involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So, sir, please just answer the question if you can. From the time that you had decided to go and take this photograph to the time that you left that area and when you had taken the photograph, how long was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I passed along, took out my camera, filmed -- or, rather, took photographs, and it could not have taken longer than a minute or two before I reached the section of the road that was safer. Not even two minutes. I was taking photographs as I was walking.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And you and the car -- you were doing all of this during the period of an ABiH offensive, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I think that the offensive began a day earlier. You see the damage there. The following day I had to go to Pale and try to find a way of getting through.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And so it's correct that you did all of this during the ABiH offensive, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: This happened in that period of time, but on other occasions the situation would happen to be similar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, you see the photograph on your screen here, the photograph that you marked. You remember this photograph. And the first question I want to ask you was where exactly was this photograph taken from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: The memorial park is in fact a fort which was several levels. I clambered up next to this wall, took my photograph and then went away from that spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And I take it the fact that you were able to clamber up onto this level, this fort was controlled by the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes. The fort was on the top of Vrace and was under the control of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And you would agree with me, sir, that from this level of the fort there is -- there appears in this photograph, at least, to be a commanding view of the city of Sarajevo, at least a part of the city of Sarajevo, doesn't there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes. One can see a good part of the town of Sarajevo, but it was very difficult to approach the fort and there was a constant danger. One exposed oneself to great risk in trying to get there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: When you went up to the fort were you accompanied by Sarajevo-Romanija Corps soldiers when you went to take this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Very close by on this side, behind there, there's a road. I don't recall who it was who came with me. I climbed up to the fort on this side, and I took photographs. I knew that there was no one there and I wanted to have photographs for my documentation. The Sarajevo-Romanija Corps did not have any soldiers there. There were no pillboxes, bunkers, or anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sir, with respect, that's not really the answer to the question I asked. I'm asking when you went up to the location from where you took the photograph, were you accompanied by soldiers? Were you accompanied by men in uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I wasn't accompanied by anyone. I alone climbed up to one part of the fort and took a photograph there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And you went there alone and I remember you telling the Court that you never carried a weapon; is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes. I never carried a weapon. I reached this spot alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And were you wearing a uniform on the day you took this photograph on top of the fort?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I don't recall exactly. I rarely wore my uniform. Only on occasions when delegations were expected or something of the sort. I did not like wearing a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sir, you went up to this area of the fort, without a uniform, or at least you don't remember wearing a uniform, without a weapon, that was under constant danger and took photographs; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sir, you see on this photograph these square holes, the square dugouts in the wall there? You see them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes, I do, and I recognise them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And, sir, you would agree given the rectangular or the -- well, the rectangular shape of these holes that these holes were not caused by shell or grenade fire, were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. These are windows that were once part of the fort. This is a memorial park which once had a plaque bearing the names of people who were killed in World War II.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it correct that on occasion Sarajevo-Romanija Corps soldiers would fire from these -- from this location through these holes down into the city?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I never saw anyone doing that. The photograph shows that nobody had been staying there. Whether somebody would come up there and shoot from there, I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: You went to this location how many times? Was it once only, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I was there for the first time sometime in 1991. The second time I went there was when I took this photograph, but I used to pass by on this side almost every day. I had to passing by this spot in order to get from Lukavica to Grbavica or vice versa. It's an elevation on which had this fort is built, and then the road ran right next to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, you remember you also were shown a photograph, one of your photographs of the -- I think it was the faculty of science and mathematics in ABiH territory. You remember that photograph, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And on that photograph you indicated to the Court the dugout holes that you say the ABiH would use to fire, and also you indicated the markings from the return fire from the SRK forces. You remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes, I did say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, let's just concentrate on the return fire. You said in evidence that the return fire -- or the fire emanated from Grbavica. You remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Where -- where from Grbavica did the return fire emanate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Mostly the area of Grbavica, between the buildings. Some sort of rifle ammunition or they used small arms to try to neutralise the places on the building of the faculty from where shots were being fired at Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Between which buildings in Grbavica, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: These were residential buildings referred to as the pavilions, paviljoni, where people lived. Those were residential buildings. I didn't see anyone shooting, but I know that they fired at those apertures in order to neutralise the snipers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sir, you didn't see that the -- where the fire came from, but I take it that you know because it was a known fact. It was common knowledge that fire was emanating from the SRK from those positions in Grbavica; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes. From Grbavica, from that area where the Serb army was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you --

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, might I have one second.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, I don't want to -- because I want to try and speed up the -- the questioning, I just want you to confirm that you remember the photograph of the building of the faculty of mathematics, and you remember the square-cum-oblong apertures that you spoke about. You remember what they looked like, don't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I remember exactly what the building looked like, and you saw in the photograph from the inside, holes were made in the building from which snipers fired. That's how I understood your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And of course you never saw these holes being made, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Well, you could never see them making those holes because they made the holes by night, and on the next day, in the morning, we would suddenly see that snipers were firing on an area that had not been protected with screens, and then we had to protect that area with screens so that it wouldn't be seen from that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: But, sir, you don't know if the holes were made at night, do you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I know they were made at night because, for example, on one day the soldiers would count three holes, and then the next morning there'd be another one or another two. You would see that there were more holes, and you could see that best because the sniper would be firing from that building, and we would know then that they were firing on a new area. But you only had to count the holes. In the evening there would be four; in the morning there would be five. That's how we knew they had made new holes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And is that something that you yourself saw? In other words, you spent one day and you saw four holes and the next day you saw five, or was that communicated to you by soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I was there one day and I know there were four holes, and when I went down they warned me and I counted again and I found there were two new holes there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, you earlier gave evidence about Nedzarici. You remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I take it you know the area well given your -- given your role in the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps and your excursions throughout the front lines; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes. I knew those lines quite well. Only some time has elapsed, so I need to recall. I need to have my memory jogged.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And I take it that you also know that there was a building or should I say a complex known as the school for blind children in Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I know that building was there. I hadn't gone there often before the war. When I went there during the war, nobody pointed out that building to me, but I was passing by. I saw an interesting scene of ruined building. Somebody told me an elderly man was living there in the basement, and then I took that photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not talking about the photograph concerning the elderly man. When you say, with respect to the school for blind children, when you say you hadn't gone there often during the war, did you visit the school for blind children during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I didn't see that school because I wasn't paying attention to that. I wasn't thinking about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: But you know, don't you, sir, that the school for blind children was under control of the VRS, or the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I assume it was, but I didn't think about it. I didn't go into that school. I know more or less where it is, but I don't know much about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, sir, I want to show you --

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I want to play a -- I want to show you a still -- show the Court a still from a clip. It will be on e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sir, on your screen you see a building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And that is -- that is one of the buildings of the school for blind children in Nedzarici, is it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I can't be sure. I know there were some school buildings there. I didn't pay attention to that building in the war. I may have passed by it, but there were many similar buildings in Sarajevo, many schools, so I didn't really -- it didn't really register that that was that building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: But do you accept that -- you accept -- you accept the possibility that this indeed is a building from the school for the blind children, don't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I don't know, because I never entered that building. I have passed through Nedzarici. There are many ruined buildings there. Whether this is the building, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: In any case I want to draw your attention to the right-hand side of the building. If you look at the right-hand side of the building, you will see the side facade that is partly covered in the photograph by some trees. Do you see that there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes, yes, you can see something black there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Let's just be clear. On the right-hand side of the building you'll see the right-hand facade which is a grey, a greyish colour of the building, and you'll see that it's partly obscured by -- at least obscured on the photograph by some trees. That's the side I'm drawing your attention to. Are we clear, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes. And I observe between the branches something black on the facade.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes. And I'm just wondering if the -- if the -- if the clip can be scrolled so we can see the top part of the building. Is that possible? Very well. Sir, you spoke about these black -- the black marks on the facade. You will see at the middle of the -- you will agree with me in the middle you will see three of those black marks; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes. You can see something. It's not very clear, but you can see something, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And then if you go -- if you cast your eyes upwards from those three black marks, you will see at the very top a beginning of another similar black mark; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes. You can see something. I don't know whether it's leaves, but there is a mark. It's either a mark on the facade or a branch. In any case, there's something there, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sir, I suggest to you that these -- these marks that we're speaking about are holes, firstly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes, they might be, but you can't see it really clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And I also suggest to you, sir, that the apertures that you were speaking about with respect to the faculty of mathematics, that these holes are similarly apertures in that building. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: It could be, but these holes are much bigger, and you can't see it clearly. If you compare this with those holes, I don't exclude the possibility, but this is quite different. This is something that's much bigger. No sniper would come and stand in a big hole, 2 by 2, and fire from there. You can't see very well. I can't really confirm that this is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sir, I have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, twice the witness has said something has been broken open. He said twice something has been broken open when talking about this. These words are quite clear. Something has been broken open. He said it twice and not once has it entered the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, we have the same problem. Witness, would you just repeat what you said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This here that you can see on the photograph, I said that something had been wrecked or torn open, as if some kind of detonation had been there. I don't know how to explain it. Destroyed, ruined. That's what we say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sir, leaving aside -- leaving aside whether snipers could use those apertures or those holes, you accept the possibility, do you not, that these are man-made holes in the -- in that facade of the building? You accept that possibility, don't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. It's hard to accept because it's not a good photograph. It might have been an explosion or something. It's really unclear. I never saw this building. There are lots of school buildings there and they all look similar. I don't know the exact location of this building. It could have been anything, as they say, but a man-made hole would be round, and this looks like some sort of smear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sir, the holes on the -- the apertures that you described and showed the Court on the faculty of mathematics were not round, were they, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Not all of them, because when they were digging the hole you could see that part of the facade had been pushed out. It depends on what the facade was like. Those holes were much smaller, and you can see that they were dug in a kind of regular pattern. But here I can't say this about these holes on this photograph. I simply don't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sir -- sir, none of those holes in the faculty of mathematics, the apertures that you spoke about, were round, were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: That's correct, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And these holes, I appreciate that the photograph is slightly blurred, these holes are not round, are they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: No, they're not. They have an irregular shape. I don't know what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd like to tender this clip into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We admit it. Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I must object. I'm not objecting, actually, but I have to say something. This photograph has been shown here for the first time, and it has not been shown to any witness so far. The Prosecution claimed that shots were fired from the roof, from the top, and now we suddenly have this photograph which completely changes the line of fire for the incident we dealt with so extensively. I don't object to its being admitted, but -- I'm not objecting, but I do wish to mention this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd like to respond. In our submission it does not change the Prosecution's theory, and in fact in our submission it bolsters it, because I'm drawing attention to the mark at the very top of the roof. That's -- that's the reason why I'm tendering this -- this still.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I said we would admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P909, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, sir, you clearly -- clearly -- you clearly know the Pale-Lukavica Road quite well, don't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes. I got to know it quite well during the war. That's all I can say.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And you would agree with me that on certain sections of that road there were positions where one could have a commanding view of the city of Sarajevo. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I didn't look to see that. I didn't think about it. It's possible. I was passing through that area, and I didn't, quite simply, pay attention to that. I didn't think about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: When you, as you say, were in the command of the SRK, when you went about your business did you -- firstly, did you visit any SRK positions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes. You saw the buildings that I entered that we showed at the beginning. Depending on the events that had taken place, that's where I went, to those places.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Did you visit any positions on Mount Trebevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: I passed along that road, but I never entered that position. I never stood there. I never stopped there. I saw there were soldiers there, but I didn't go in and look around. There was no need.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sir, while you were driving along that road you saw that there were SRK soldiers along at that road; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Yes. I saw soldiers passing by.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I want to now show you another clip. It's a ...

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, sir, since you've travelled that road frequently in your time with the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, you would agree that this position that we saw here was -- was along that road, wasn't it? Somewhere along that road where one had a view of the city?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Possibly. I can't be a hundred per cent certain. Probably, but I don't know. I never stood in that spot, saw the town like that. I was mainly passing by. And who was there exactly I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Well, I'm not suggesting that you yourself went to that position, but it's -- you would agree that it's -- it's most likely a position from the Lukavica-Pale road. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: That's possible, but I can't be a hundred per cent certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And you know that that road and if it is indeed that position that I suggested to you, that would have been controlled by the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T-41
utterances.text: Probably. I don't know. It's possible, but I'm telling you I'm not a hundred per cent certain that that's it. I can't really recognise what part of town this is although I know Sarajevo quite well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sir. Sir, please just listen to the question very carefully. I'm asking you that if -- if we take it as this is the position that I'm suggesting to you on the Trebevic -- on the Lukavica-Pale road, then that position would have been controlled by the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the same question is being asked for the third time. The witness has already replied twice, and now the same question is being put again. I won't quote the witness's response, but now we're hearing the same question for the third time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, it's not at all the same question, but I can just ask -- I'll ask it another way that will be less complicated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ask it -- ask it tomorrow. We're going to take the break now.
